info.name: Assignment Bridge API
info.description:
REST API for **Assignment Bridge** - students post assignments and get help from verified experts.

### Roles
`STUDENT` | `EXPERT` | `ADMIN`

### Auth
On `POST /auth/login` the server sets `accessToken` (15m) and `refreshToken` (7d) as httpOnly cookies **and** returns both in the response body. Protected routes accept either the cookie or an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

The login request has a test script that stores the tokens into the collection variables, so `Get Me` and the admin routes work right after you log in.

### Variables
| variable | default |
| --- | --- |
| `serverUrl` | `http://localhost:4000` |
| `baseUrl` | `{{serverUrl}}/api/v1` |
| `accessToken` | filled by the login test script |
| `refreshToken` | filled by the login test script |
| `expertId` | id of the `experts` row you want to approve/reject |

### Error shape
Every failure goes through the global error handler:
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "statusCode": 400,
  "name": "Error",
  "message": "...",
  "error": { },
  "stack": "..."
}
```
`name`, `error` and `stack` are only populated when `NODE_ENV=development`.

request.description: Returns `{ "message": "Hello Assignment Bridge V1.0!" }` with `200`. Use it to confirm the server and Redis connection came up.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Student signup, login and password reset. All bodies are validated with zod, so a bad field returns `400` with the zod issue list in `message`.

request.description:
Step 1 of signup. Nothing is written to Postgres yet - the hashed user and a 6-digit OTP are parked in Redis under `newUser:<email>` and `registerOtp:<email>` for 1 hour. Finish with `Verify Register OTP`.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required, 3-255 chars |
| `email` | string | required, valid email, lowercased server-side |
| `password` | string | required, 6-64 chars |
| `role` | enum | optional - `STUDENT` \| `EXPERT` \| `ADMIN` |

**Note:** `role` passes validation but the service ignores it and always creates a `STUDENT`. Experts sign up through `Expert > Register Expert` instead.

**Errors**
- `400` email already registered (`"User already exists, please login"`)
- `400` email belongs to a Google account
- `500` Redis write failed

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Step 2 of signup. Consumes the OTP, creates the `users` row with `emailVerified: true`, `role: STUDENT`, and an attached `students` row (`institution: ""`, `academicLevel: ""`). Both Redis keys are deleted afterwards.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email |
| `otp` | string | required, exactly 6 chars |

**Returns** the created user (password omitted) with its nested `student`.

**Errors**
- `400` OTP expired / not found
- `400` invalid OTP
- `400` cached user data expired

exec: // Store the tokens so the protected requests in this collection just work.

request.description:
Works for every role - the JWT carries `{ userId, name, email, role }`.

Sets two httpOnly cookies (`accessToken` 15m, `refreshToken` 7d) and also returns them in `data`. The attached test script copies them into the `accessToken` / `refreshToken` collection variables.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email |
| `password` | string | required, 6-64 chars |

**Errors**
- `400` user does not exist
- `400` account is Google-only and has no password
- `400` wrong password

**Protected** - `STUDENT`, `EXPERT` or `ADMIN`.

Returns the full user row (password omitted) with both the `student` and `expert` relations included; the one that does not apply to the caller comes back `null`.

Token resolution order in the auth middleware:
1. `accessToken` cookie
2. `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
3. raw `Authorization` header value

If the access token is missing but a valid `refreshToken` cookie is present, the middleware silently mints a fresh access token and sets the cookie on the response.

**Errors**
- `401` no token at all, or the token failed verification
- `403` role not allowed / account is `BLOCK`ed
- `404` token is valid but the user row is gone

request.description:
Stores a 6-digit OTP at `forgetPasswordOtp:<lowercased email>` in Redis for 5 minutes.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email |

**Errors**
- `400` user does not exist
- `500` Redis write failed

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Consumes the reset OTP and re-hashes the password.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email |
| `newPassword` | string | required, 6-64 chars |
| `otp` | string | required, exactly 6 chars |

> **Known issues in the current implementation** (documented, not fixed):
> 1. The service first requires a `newUser:<email>` Redis key, which only exists during a pending *registration* - so this endpoint returns `400 "User data has expired"` for any normal reset.
> 2. The OTP lookup uses the raw `payload.email` while `Forget Password` wrote the key with a lowercased email, so a mixed-case address misses the key.

**Errors**
- `400` cached user data expired (see note 1)
- `400` OTP expired
- `400` invalid OTP

item.name: Expert
item.description:
Expert onboarding and admin verification. An expert is a `users` row with `role: EXPERT` plus an `experts` row holding their academic details, uploaded documents and `verificationStatus`.

`verificationStatus` starts at `PENDING` and an admin moves it to `APPROVE` or `REJECT` exactly once.

request.description:
Step 1 of expert onboarding. Nothing hits Postgres yet - the hashed user goes to `expertRegister:<email>` and a 6-digit OTP to `expertRegisterOtp:<email>`, both for 1 hour. Finish with `Verify Expert`.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required |
| `email` | string | required |
| `password` | string | required |

**Note:** this route has no zod middleware, so field rules are not enforced server-side - the email is also used verbatim (not lowercased), unlike the student flow.

**Errors**
- `409` email already registered
- `500` Redis write failed

response.name: 200 OK

formdata.value:
{
  "email": "{{expertEmail}}",
  "otp": "123456",
  "university": "University of Dhaka",
  "department": "Computer Science & Engineering",
  "ratePerAssignment": 1500,
  "bio": "CSE graduate, 5 years of experience helping with data structures and algorithms assignments."
}
formdata.description:
**Required.** A JSON *string* - the server does `JSON.parse(req.body.body)`. Do not send these as separate form fields.

| field | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | must match the address used at register |
| `otp` | string | 6 digits |
| `university` | string | required |
| `department` | string | required |
| `ratePerAssignment` | number | required, price per assignment |
| `bio` | string | optional, stored as `null` when empty |

Up to **5** files (degree certificate, ID, transcript...). Held in memory by multer, then streamed to Cloudinary under the `expert-documents` folder with `resource_type: auto`. Each upload is persisted on the expert row as `{ url, publicId }`.

request.description:
Step 2 of expert onboarding - **`multipart/form-data`**, not JSON.

Let Postman set the `Content-Type` boundary itself; do not add the header manually.

Consumes the OTP, uploads the documents to Cloudinary, then creates the `users` row (`role: EXPERT`, `emailVerified: true`) with its `experts` row at `isVerified: false` / `verificationStatus: PENDING`. Both Redis keys are deleted afterwards.

The expert cannot take work until an admin runs `Approve / Reject Expert` - grab the returned `expert.id` into the `expertId` collection variable for that call.

**Errors**
- `400` OTP expired or registration not found
- `400` invalid OTP
- `409` email got registered in the meantime
- `500` Cloudinary upload failed

response.body:

request.description:
**Protected - `ADMIN` only.** Log in as an admin first so the test script fills `accessToken`.

One endpoint handles both decisions via `status`.

**Body**
| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expertId` | string | required - the `experts.id` (not `users.id`) |
| `status` | string | required - `APPROVE` or `REJECT`, uppercased server-side so `approve` also works |
| `reason` | string | **required when `status` is `REJECT`**, ignored otherwise |

- `APPROVE` -> `isVerified: true`, `verificationStatus: APPROVE`
- `REJECT` -> `isVerified: false`, `verificationStatus: REJECT`, `rejectionReason: <reason>`

To reject, send:
```json
{
  "expertId": "{{expertId}}",
  "status": "REJECT",
  "reason": "Uploaded certificate is not readable."
}
```

**Note:** the decision is one-shot - an expert already `APPROVE`d or `REJECT`ed returns `400`, there is no re-review endpoint. Also, the response `data` is always `null`; re-read the expert through `Get Me` as that user to confirm.

**Errors**
- `400` missing `expertId` / `status`, invalid `status`, missing `reason` on reject, or already decided
- `401` not logged in
- `403` caller is not an `ADMIN`
- `404` expert not found

response.name: 403 Forbidden
